statement: Treat a transport or infrastructure graph as measured data: document its provenance, geometry, edge semantics, resolution, temporal state, and linkage uncertainty before using it to generate a spatial prediction.
inapplicable: Purely abstract graph problems where edges and weights are fully specified by the prompt
procedure: Name the source, extraction date, coordinate reference system, and geographic extent.
Define vertices, directed edges, local connectors, barriers, and every edge-cost unit.
Record speed, congestion, turn, access, and time-of-day assumptions where relevant.
State grid or graph resolution and quantify discretization error.
Document event-linkage and coordinate uncertainty.
Validate sampled routes or graph relations against external observations.
Version the exact graph and event table used by the model.
positive_pattern: A road profile stores a directed travel-time graph with map provenance, local-road connectors, time-dependent edge costs, held-out route checks, and coordinate uncertainty for every incident.
forbidden: Calling Euclidean edge length travel time
Manual map encoding without reproducible rules
Omitting grid size or map extent
Treating uncertain series linkage as ground truth
Using a colorful map as graph validation

statement: Adapt a standard spatial model with a domain-specific graph metric only after proving that the metric's units, behavior, topology, and calibration match the mechanism represented by the model.
inapplicable: Cases where straight-line distance is the explicit target quantity
procedure: State the real movement or interaction mechanism.
Define the metric or cost and its units.
Check nonnegativity, identity, symmetry when intended, and triangle behavior.
Calibrate edge costs with observed routes or interaction data.
Compare against Euclidean, Manhattan, and simpler graph baselines.
Re-estimate all parameters inherited from another metric.
Test rankings under omitted barriers, modes, and temporal conditions.
positive_pattern: A road-kernel model uses observed directed travel times, reselects bandwidth under that cost, and demonstrates improvement over Euclidean and uncalibrated network distance.
forbidden: Changing distance while retaining old hyperparameters
Equating length with time
Adding domain terminology without behavioral calibration
Assuming a metric is better because its heatmap looks plausible

statement: Evolve a spatial probability field only with a representation that preserves nonnegativity, normalization, spatial dependence, and temporal information available at the forecast origin.
inapplicable: Unnormalized scores explicitly presented only as relative utilities
procedure: Define whether the output is a density, intensity, risk score, or rank.
Choose a graph or spatial kernel with boundary-aware normalization.
Specify how recency and elapsed time enter.
Tune bandwidth and decay with rolling-origin scoring.
Use a constrained evolution, log-density, softmax, point-process, or other probability-preserving representation.
Verify nonnegativity and total mass at every forecast origin.
Compare with recency-only, uniform, historical-frequency, and static-KDE baselines.
positive_pattern: A graph heat-kernel intensity is tuned on prior forecast origins, remains nonnegative and normalized after prediction, and beats simple spatial and temporal baselines on held-out events.
forbidden: Unconstrained pointwise linear extrapolation of densities
Empirical bandwidth without a disclosed loss
Using the future event time as an input
Ignoring boundary mass and neighboring-cell dependence

statement: Combine multiple required schemes or objectives through a target-consistent, unit-aware probabilistic or decision rule; do not call side-by-side outputs, incomparable sums, or unions model fusion.
inapplicable: Prompts explicitly requesting separate independent outputs with no combined decision
procedure: Write the target, horizon, unit, scale, and decision role for every scheme or objective.
Determine whether outputs estimate the same quantity or represent competing values.
For a common target, calibrate and combine scores with a justified probabilistic method.
For different targets, define a joint latent model or keep them separate until an explicit decision-loss layer.
For objectives, preserve native units, disclose normalization, and elicit or stress-test preferences.
Describe how every extra evidence source changes variables or priors.
Tune fusion only inside training folds or pre-policy data.
Compare the combined system against each component under operational loss and alternative preferences.
positive_pattern: The 2010 case needs a joint or decision-layer link between residence and next-event fields; a tourism model should first expose the economic-social-environmental frontier, then select a policy with documented stakeholder preferences.
forbidden: Calling all hotspots a combined prediction
Adding incomparable monetary or index scales without validation
Using unrelated rankings as welfare weights without sensitivity
Using test outcomes to choose fusion weights
Assuming more components automatically improve decisions

statement: Keep targets, objectives, metrics, welfare values, cash flows, and decisions distinct, and label every output by definition, unit, horizon, conditioning information, and intended use.
procedure: List all requested and intermediate quantities.
Define one variable or decision quantity for each target, objective, cash flow, and welfare measure.
Draw dependencies and conversion edges.
Assign target-specific data, metrics, and uncertainty.
Separate cash revenue from transfer payments, avoided cost, and nonmarket welfare.
Translate outputs into decisions only after stating loss, preferences, and constraints.
Bind summary, figures, conclusion, and memo to one result dictionary.
positive_pattern: A system reports distinct next-event and residence distributions, or distinct economic, resident, ecological, budget, and total-policy quantities, with explicit links and no name drift.
forbidden: Using one target's validation for another
Calling welfare benefit revenue
Changing weighted total benefit into social benefit in a memo
Presenting priority or utility as absolute probability
Dropping units or horizons

statement: Probe geometric objectives with small adversarial perturbations, then replace unstable formulations with metric-space estimators whose robustness, uncertainty, and relation to the claimed geometry are explicitly tested.
inapplicable: Exact deterministic geometry with noiseless complete inputs
procedure: Construct minimal configurations with known solutions.
Perturb one point, edge, or weight and measure output movement.
Identify the source of non-identifiability or instability.
Choose a Fréchet mean, medoid, robust loss, regularized fit, or distributional estimator appropriate to the metric space.
Name the quantity actually optimized.
Bootstrap or analytically estimate uncertainty.
Test outliers, multimodality, and grid resolution.
positive_pattern: A road-space center is introduced after a perturbation exposes circumcircle instability, then compared with medoid and robust-loss alternatives under bootstrap event resampling.
forbidden: Keeping an unstable fit because it is visually familiar
Calling a center-plus-mean-radius an optimized circle fit
Showing one counterexample without testing the replacement
Ignoring multimodal configurations

statement: Evaluate sequential spatial predictions with leakage-free rolling origins, target-appropriate scores, explicit baselines, and operational search-cost metrics rather than one final-event picture.
inapplicable: Single deterministic instances with no historical sequence or external cases
procedure: Define each forecast origin and freeze all available information.
Predict multiple later events one at a time or in blocks.
Tune parameters only on earlier origins or nested folds.
For probabilistic outputs, report log score, Brier-style scores where appropriate, rank, and calibration.
For search outputs, report area or cost searched before target, hit rate at fixed area, and cumulative search curves.
Compare with uniform, historical-frequency, recency, Euclidean, and scheme-specific baselines.
Report results by case and aggregate with uncertainty.
positive_pattern: Every event after a minimum history is forecast using only prior information; the method is compared with simple baselines on log score, target percentile, and area searched before hit.
forbidden: Using the held-out event time
Testing only the final event
Scoring known residences on a surface fitted with all events and calling it predictive
Undefined nontrivial probability
Grid-dependent ratios without resolution analysis

statement: Make reliability case- or policy-specific by testing scope assumptions, calibrating uncertainty, quantifying joint sensitivity and decision stability, and abstaining when the model is outside its validated regime.
procedure: Convert every scope assumption into a measurable diagnostic.
Estimate predictive or decision uncertainty with a justified method.
Test data, parameter, model-form, preference, time, and implementation uncertainty jointly.
Report calibration, coverage, robust feasibility, or regret as appropriate to the target.
Rank factor importance over all plausible inputs, not only selected levers.
Define warning levels and failure modes.
Set an abstention or fallback rule before deployment.
Carry warnings and uncertainty into the stakeholder deliverable.
positive_pattern: A case profile reports coverage and linkage sensitivity; a tourism policy reports a robust visitor range and policy-switch thresholds across demand, weights, delays, and ecological uncertainty.
forbidden: Generic limitations without a case test
One-factor plots called robustness
Confidence language from one chart
A precise policy optimum without uncertainty
New unsupported forecasts in a memo
Hiding uncertainty in future-work prose

statement: Design every geospatial field as an auditable decision map with location reference, physical scale, numeric legend, observed and held-out markers, uncertainty, and cumulative search regions.
inapplicable: Pure conceptual schematics that make no quantitative spatial claim
procedure: Show coordinate system or recognizable geography and a scale bar.
Overlay the relevant network and distinguish training from held-out events.
Use a perceptually ordered, color-accessible palette with a numeric colorbar and units.
State whether values are probability, density, intensity, score, rank, or distance.
Draw calibrated contours or cumulative area bands tied to decisions.
Show uncertainty, stability, or ensemble spread.
Mark the target without covering the underlying field.
Use aligned scales for case and baseline comparisons.
positive_pattern: A next-event map overlays prior events and the held-out target on a calibrated density, adds 50/80/95 percent search contours, a scale bar, numeric legend, and uncertainty band, then places a baseline map beside it.
forbidden: Rainbow heatmaps without numeric values
No coordinates or scale
Color bands described as search speed
Unlabeled 3D surfaces
Different case scales hidden behind the same colors
No indication of train versus test points

statement: Trace every official Problem B clause through definitions, data, model or scheme, combination rule, feedback, validation, adaptation, uncertainty, and the final stakeholder answer.
procedure: Extract the prompt into atomic deliverables.
Map each deliverable to a target, objective, decision, and section.
Show how each model uses data and what it outputs.
Name combination rules and preserve definitions and units.
Trace extra evidence and revenue expenditures through state changes.
Attach verification and reliability evidence to each result.
Validate transfer claims with location-specific data.
Bind summary, conclusion, and memo to the same result dictionary.
Close in prompt order with uncertainty and warnings.
positive_pattern: A requirement matrix covers model, objectives, constraints, feedback budget, sensitivity importance, validated destination adaptation, less-visited attraction policy, and a memo whose values are generated from the final result table.
forbidden: Counting model names as coverage
A workflow branch with no output
Calling maps or scalar sums valid combination without tests
Expenditure prose with no feedback edge
Memo numbers absent from the model
Leaving reliability as generic prose

statement: Use quantitative success, novelty, rigor, generalizability, and reliability adjectives only after naming the target, test, comparator, metric, scope, and uncertainty that support them.
procedure: Name the exact target or objective and evaluation status.
Report the metric, units, baseline, and acceptance rule.
State the dataset, forecast origin, destination, or policy scenario.
Report uncertainty and sensitivity to material assumptions.
Use strong, accurate, global, robust, scalable, innovative, obvious, and easy only at a predeclared evidence threshold.
Describe failures under the same metric.
Run a cross-section number and target-name audit.
positive_pattern: A spatial model reports held-out rank and search area; a policy model reports dominance, robust feasibility, regret, destination holdout performance, and confidence bounds before claiming generalizability.
forbidden: Good fit without a loss
Very nontrivial probability
Global Pareto without a front or dominance test
Obviously realistic because an assumed curve peaks
Scalable from copied curve shapes
Robust from one-factor plots
New memo forecasts without derivation

statement: Use a geographic profile only to prioritize limited resources under explicit costs; never present location priority as evidence of guilt, and audit privacy, false-positive burden, and geographic or demographic bias.
inapplicable: Low-stakes simulations with no real person, property, or service impact
procedure: Define the allowed decision and prohibited interpretation.
Separate event risk, residence likelihood, person suspicion, and resource allocation.
Specify false-positive, false-negative, travel, privacy, and opportunity costs.
Limit data to necessary and lawful evidence with retention controls.
Measure burden by region and relevant population groups.
Require human review and corroborating evidence.
Provide audit logs, contestability, and an abstention path.
Phrase recommendations as search priorities, not guilt probabilities.
positive_pattern: The system ranks geographic areas for time-bounded patrol allocation, reports expected area and false-positive burden, prohibits person-level inference, and requires independent evidence before investigative escalation.
forbidden: Treating a hotspot as probable guilt
Targeting demographic proxies without necessity and bias tests
Claiming police can easily locate a person from an in-sample map
Omitting privacy and contestability
Continuing after scope diagnostics fail

statement: Select graph-distance computation and caching from explicit query volume, latency, memory, update frequency, and accuracy requirements; do not precompute every grid-cell pair without a measured tradeoff.
inapplicable: Small fixed graphs where exact all-pairs storage is demonstrably trivial
procedure: Count vertices, edges, grid cells, sources, targets, and expected queries.
Estimate time and memory complexity of all-pairs, repeated single-source, multi-source, landmark, contraction, and on-demand caching options.
Account for graph updates and invalidation.
Measure accuracy loss from grid coarsening or approximation.
Benchmark representative cases.
Choose the simplest method meeting latency and memory limits.
Report how computational choices affect final rankings and decisions.
positive_pattern: A benchmark compares exact on-demand Dijkstra, landmark approximation, and cached multi-source queries across grid resolutions, then chooses the lowest-memory method meeting response-time and ranking-error limits.
forbidden: Storing all cell pairs by default
Claiming a finer grid is better without convergence
Reporting algorithm names without runtime and memory
Ignoring dynamic edge updates
Optimizing runtime without checking decision changes

statement: Build a policy-parameter ledger that records exact provenance, unit, scale convention, transformation, estimation method, uncertainty, temporal/geographic scope, and downstream uses for every input.
inapplicable: Prompt-specified dimensionless constants used only in a toy derivation
procedure: Assign every parameter a stable ID and definition.
Cite the exact table, field, date, geography, and retrieval method.
Normalize percent, proportion, currency-year, per-capita, total, and million-unit conventions.
Document transformations and missing-data handling.
For estimates, state sample, loss, fitting algorithm, diagnostics, and uncertainty.
Mark transfer limits and re-estimation triggers.
Trace each parameter into equations, code, plots, sensitivity, and recommendations.
positive_pattern: Tax is stored once as a decimal with a display-percent formatter; every fitted elasticity includes a source dataset, confidence interval, and destination scope, and unit tests reject mixed conventions.
forbidden: Source listed only as Government or Estimate
Using 5, 0.05, and 0.58 without definitions
Unknown currency base year
Copying parameters to another city without a scope check
Publishing more precision than calibration supports

statement: Distinguish Pareto analysis, scalar optimization, and game equilibrium: compute the feasible nondominated set before selecting one policy, and define players and payoffs before making game-theoretic claims.
inapplicable: Single-objective problems with no competing values or strategic agents
procedure: Define each objective in its native direction and unit.
Define the feasible set and verify bounds.
Generate nondominated solutions using epsilon constraints, weight sweeps, evolutionary methods, or another justified approach.
Check dominance and coverage of nonconvex regions.
Display the Pareto frontier and tradeoff rates.
Select a compromise only after disclosing normalization and preferences.
For games, define players, strategies, payoffs, information, and equilibrium concept.
Verify solver feasibility, multiple starts, and KKT or comparable conditions.
positive_pattern: A tourism model shows the feasible economic-resident-ecological frontier, quantifies tradeoffs, obtains stakeholder preference ranges, and then selects a robust policy; it uses game language only if attractions have explicit strategic decisions and payoffs.
forbidden: Calling one weighted SLSQP solution the Pareto front
Pairwise curves with no nondominated points
Global optimality from one local solver run
Rank weights treated as objective truth
Game terminology without players or payoffs

statement: Monetize hidden social or environmental effects only with dimensionally valid shadow prices, causal links, uncertainty, and a double-count audit; keep cash, transfers, avoided costs, and welfare separate.
inapplicable: Multi-objective analysis that deliberately retains native nonmonetary units
procedure: Draw the causal chain from activity to physical or social effect.
Define the valuation perspective and unit.
Select a cited shadow price or estimate it from relevant data.
Normalize currency year, geography, and population basis.
Propagate physical and valuation uncertainty.
Separate government cash, resident income, transfers, avoided damage, and nonmarket welfare.
Check overlap among objective terms.
Test results with native-unit multi-objective analysis and alternative valuations.
positive_pattern: Carbon tonnes are estimated linearly from mode-specific activity, valued with an uncertain social cost of carbon, and kept separate from tax transfers; resident satisfaction remains a surveyed objective unless a defensible willingness-to-pay estimate exists.
forbidden: Declaring an arbitrary index value USD
Subtracting spending as if it automatically removes equal damage
Calling social welfare cash revenue
Per-person factors multiplied by squared people
Missing currency factors
Double counting resident income and satisfaction

statement: Model sustainability as a dynamic feedback system in which policies and expenditures change demand, capacity, resident welfare, infrastructure, and ecology over explicit time lags; do not infer long-run sustainability from one static optimum.
inapplicable: Explicitly one-period allocation tasks with no future-state claim
procedure: Define state variables and decision periods.
Model demand, booking, construction, maintenance, ecological, and behavioral lags.
Conserve budget and map expenditure to state transitions.
Include depreciation, capacity saturation, and delayed benefits.
Optimize a multi-period objective or policy rule.
Simulate baseline, stress, and implementation-delay scenarios.
Re-estimate or update as new observations arrive.
Report transient, steady-state, and worst-case outcomes.
positive_pattern: Annual visitor caps, taxes, and reinvestment allocations update infrastructure condition, attraction capacity, resident satisfaction, ecological state, and next-year demand before the policy is re-optimized.
forbidden: Instantaneous full-information response called sustainable
An expenditure list disconnected from equations
Ignoring decay and seasonality while forecasting decades
One-period optimum presented as a permanent cap
No budget conservation

statement: Validate destination or context transfer by re-estimating changed mechanisms from local data and testing outcomes or policy rankings; similar curves from copied formulas do not establish generalizability.
inapplicable: Pure scenario illustrations explicitly not claimed as validation
procedure: Create a transfer schema for geography, institutions, behavior, economy, ecology, infrastructure, and data quality.
Identify invariant and destination-specific mechanisms.
Acquire local calibration data and re-estimate specific parameters.
Define local constraints and decision costs.
Test predictions or policy rankings against observed local outcomes.
Compare with a local baseline and source-only transfer.
Use a third context or leave-one-context-out evaluation when possible.
Document failure and nontransfer conditions.
positive_pattern: A Juneau model is re-estimated with Jiuzhaigou visitor, capacity, resident, price, seasonality, and ecology data, evaluated on observed years, and then tested on a third overtourism destination.
forbidden: Changing only tax and weights
Copying elasticities because cities seem similar
Curve-shape similarity called scalability
Qualitative destination tables without model consequences
Reducing ecological weight without local evidence

statement: Run a deterministic mathematical preflight before numerical optimization: verify dimensions, algebra, limiting behavior, feasible domains, objective naming, and solver diagnostics against the implementation.
applicability: All equation-based and numerical Problem B models
procedure: Build a symbol table with units and scales.
Simplify composite formulas symbolically and identify cancellations.
Check exponents and logarithm arguments are dimensionless.
Evaluate zero, boundary, large-input, and monotonicity cases.
Reconcile constraints, search bounds, and plot domains.
Compare printed equations with code on hand-calculated fixtures.
Run multiple starts and record solver status, feasibility residuals, gradients, and convergence.
Bind all reported results to reproducible outputs.
positive_pattern: Preflight catches a cancelled congestion term, percent/proportion mismatch, squared-person emission error, and conflicting visitor bounds before the optimizer is allowed to produce policy recommendations.
forbidden: Optimization before unit checks
Logarithms of dimensional quantities
Per-person coefficients times squared populations
A solver result without status or residuals
Different domains in equations, code, and figures
Manual copying of final values

statement: Close every revenue-expenditure feedback loop with conserved cash, explicit allocations, lagged state changes, and re-optimization; a prose spending list does not satisfy a feedback requirement.
inapplicable: Prompts that request only a descriptive spending proposal with no model feedback
procedure: Separate cash revenue, transfers, avoided costs, and welfare.
Write the budget identity and allocation constraints.
Assign each expenditure to a measurable state or parameter.
Model implementation lag, diminishing return, depreciation, and uncertainty.
Update capacity, costs, demand, satisfaction, or ecology.
Recompute objectives and constraints in the next period.
Compare reinvestment allocations with a no-feedback baseline.
Carry budget and outcome numbers into the memo.
positive_pattern: Tourist taxes fund explicit infrastructure, ecological, and community allocations; each changes next-year states and the model re-optimizes visitor policy under a balanced budget.
forbidden: Calling virtual social welfare revenue
An expenditure category with no amount
No edge from spending to model state
Assuming every dollar of spending removes a dollar of damage
No second optimization

statement: Visualize multi-objective decisions with feasible nondominated solutions, native units, tradeoff direction, selected policy, uncertainty, and preference sensitivity; use constraint and sensitivity plots that match the actual model domain.
inapplicable: Single-objective plots with one clear unit and no tradeoff
procedure: Plot the feasible nondominated set or frontier and distinguish dominated points.
Label each objective's unit and direction.
Mark the selected compromise and preference or weight rationale.
Show how the selection moves under alternative weights and uncertainty.
For constraints, use exact decision variables, bounds, and slack units.
For sensitivity, show elasticities, global importance, interactions, or decision-switch thresholds.
Use aligned small multiples and accessible palettes.
Reconcile all figure domains and values with text and code.
positive_pattern: A frontier plot marks feasible nondominated tourism policies, the selected council policy, uncertainty envelopes, and weight-sensitivity paths; companion heatmaps show exact constraint slack over the solver bounds.
forbidden: Pairwise curves labeled Pareto without points
Radar area used as factor importance
Constraint heatmap axes that differ from equations
No optimum marker
Mixed scales without normalization disclosure
Schematic curves presented as empirical validation

statement: Ground public-policy objectives, weights, thresholds, and recommendations in affected stakeholder evidence and report distributional effects; mathematical scalarization does not create social legitimacy.
inapplicable: Pure technical optimization with one owner and no affected external parties
procedure: Identify residents, workers, businesses, visitors, government, ecosystems, and vulnerable groups.
Separate outcomes and constraints by stakeholder.
Elicit preferences, minimum standards, or acceptable ranges with documented methods.
Audit who receives revenue and who bears cost, crowding, displacement, or ecological harm.
Test alternative weights and veto constraints.
Report distributional and equity outcomes alongside totals.
Provide participation, review, and revision mechanisms.
Qualify recommendations when stakeholder data are absent.
positive_pattern: Resident surveys set minimum satisfaction, ecological limits are hard constraints, businesses and workers receive separate income outcomes, and the council sees how policies shift benefits and burdens across groups.
forbidden: State rankings used as stakeholder preferences
Aggregate total benefit hiding losers
Equal visitor allocation across unequal sites
Tax recommendations without incidence analysis
Environmental neglect justified by a small weight
Survey language without survey data

statement: When generative AI assists a competition paper, disclose use at artifact level and independently verify every affected equation, code path, translation, citation, figure, and policy claim before submission.
applicability: AI-assisted research, writing, coding, translation, visualization, and memo preparation
procedure: Record tool, model/version when known, date, prompt, output, and purpose.
Map each AI interaction to the final file, section, equation, or code block.
Record whether suggestions were accepted, modified, or rejected.
Independently check mathematics, units, citations, data, and factual claims.
Run tests on AI-reviewed or generated code and resolve every warning.
Have a competent human review translations and stakeholder language.
Scan the final paper for untraceable AI-derived claims.
Generate the required AI report without treating disclosure as correctness evidence.
positive_pattern: The ledger links a code-review prompt to a commit and passing tests, a translation prompt to independently reviewed paragraphs, and a concept prompt to equations verified from primary sources.
forbidden: Prompt disclosure with no final-artifact mapping
Leaving AI-flagged code issues unresolved
Generalizing AI-translated phrasing as source-authored style
Citing fabricated or unchecked sources
Assuming disclosure validates content
